info.title: MICROSERVICE-PROD-Get Cross Channel By Param1-spec
info.description: The Cross Channel Authentication API facilitates secure access to banking services by retrieving authentication information for a specific party based on a unique parameter. This endpoint is essential for applications requiring user validation across multiple channels. Typically used by financial institutions and third-party developers, it ensures that only authorized entities can engage in transactions. The API enhances user experience by streamlining the authentication process across various banking platforms.

get.description: This endpoint retrieves the authentication details for a specific party identified by PARTY-600045. It allows developers to access information related to the party's authentication status, facilitating integrations with external systems and user verification processes.

requestBody.description: Request body for retrieving authentication details related to a specific party identified by PARTY-600045. This should contain necessary authentication details in JSON format.

200.description: Request was successful and the resource was retrieved.

GetCrossChannelByParam1Request.title: Cross-Channel Party Authentication Request Body
GetCrossChannelByParam1Request.description: This schema represents the request body for party authentication in a cross-channel operation.

GetCrossChannelByParam1Response_200.title: Party Authentication Response

channel.description: The communication channel used for the authentication.

authenticationLevel.description: The level of authentication that has been performed.

recordStatus.description: The current status of the record.

version.description: The version of the authentication record.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the record was last updated.

correlationId.description: Identifier for tracking the request/response correlation.

bearerAuth.description: Authentication scheme using Bearer tokens with JSON Web Tokens (JWT). This method allows clients to authenticate by including a token in the Authorization header of their requests.
